To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the autonomic cardiac parameters of depressed patients treated with TCAs are significantly reduced as compared to those of normal control subjects.
the amitriptylin-induced decrease of heart rate variability is mainly due to its anticholinergic effects.
the heart rate variability (R-R variation) in amitriptiline-treated depressed patients was significantly decreased as compared to the control subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of amitriptylin (AT) on autonomic cardiac parameters.
the question whether the autonomic heart rate variability (R-R interval) in depressed patients is influenced by the tricyclic drug amitriptyine.
the biological and clinical significance of heart rate variability parameters (HRV) in depressed patients and in healthy subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

amitriptylne treatment of depressive patients is accompanied by a decrease in the parameters of HRV, which is largely independent from heart-rate and is mainly due to the drug's anticholinergic properties.
the results of the present investigation are in agreement with the hypothesis that TCAs exert an anticholinergic action on the heart and that this action is dose dependent.
amitriptylne, like other TCA's, has anticholinergic effects on heart rate, but the effect of TCAs on the autonomic nervous system seems to be more complex than previously thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the autonomic nervous system plays a key role in the regulation of the heart rate, especially in patients with a major depressive disorder.

the autonomic nervous system plays an important role in the regulation of heart rate, that the heart rate is a good parameter to measure the effect of antidepressant drugs on the autonomic nervous regulation of heart rate and that the effect of antidepressants on the autonomic regulation of heart rate can be detected in the electrocardiac R-R interval.
the HRV is a useful and non-invasive tool in the assessment of autonomic cardiac function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heart rate variability is a valuable tool for detecting the presence and severity of autonomic nervous system dysfunction in patients with depression and other psychiatric illnesses.
we need to do more research into the relationship between depression and heart rate variability.
the heart rate is an excellent predictor of mortality in patients with heart failure.
